newsitem.title: USA: NYS Gov Pataki seeks to strengthen muni bond bank.
newsitem.headline: NYS Gov Pataki seeks to strengthen muni bond bank.

text.p: New York State Gov George Pataki, who was criticized by the state comptroller for not giving distressed localities enough help, on Friday said he would propose strengthening the Municipal Bond Bank Agency.

The agency, which currently is limited to pool financing--raising funds for a number of municipalities--has only sold one $60 million issue that was offered in the early 1990s, state budget officials said.

The Republican governor said his new plan would enable individual municipalities to cut the cost of borrowing by issuing debt through the agency, which would be supported by an intercept of the locality's state aid and sales tax revenues.
The localities would have to win the state comptroller's recommendation and, where appropriate, get this watchdog's approval of a "corrective" plan.

Pataki's plan also would enable individual municipalities to securitize delinquent tax liens through a private trust, a step state budget officials noted some large entities, like New York City, which securitized delinquent commercial property tax liens, already have taken.

"This would provide an immediate influx of cash directly to the participating municipality from the bond sale, would increase tax collection rates, and would return chronically delinquent properties to the tax rolls," Pataki said, in prepared remarks.

The state budget officials, who declined to be named, said that the plan would redress the imbalances created when municipalities are forced to raise taxes on other entities to make up for the revenues lost from delinquent tax liens.
No estimates of how much such delinquent tax liens now amount to were immediately available.
